1.note: The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [the heads of the fathers’ families]

Here, **to the face of** represents “into the presence of.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to Moses and to the leaders]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:2. This also occurs in verses 2–5, 7–9, and 13.
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:34. This also occurs in verse 12.

2.q: אֶת אֲדֹנִ⁠י֙ צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה לָ⁠תֵ֨ת אֶת הָ⁠אָ֧רֶץ
2.note: Even though the leaders of the clan of Gilead are addressing Moses directly, they are speaking of him in the third person as **my lord** to show respect. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in a respectful form in the second person. Alternate translation: [Yahweh commanded you, sir, to give the land]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **inheritance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to be inherited]

The expression **was commanded** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and Yahweh also commanded my lord]

The leaders are using the term **brother** to describe Zelophehad as someone who was descended from the same ancestor as they were, that is, a member of their own clan. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the inheritance of Zelophehad our fellow clansman]

3.q: וְ֠⁠הָיוּ לְ⁠אֶחָ֞ד מִ⁠בְּנֵ֨י שִׁבְטֵ֥י בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ לְ⁠נָשִׁים֒
3.note: The leaders are using **they will be for wives to** as a common expression of the culture to mean “they will marry.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And they will marry men from the sons of the tribes of the sons of Israel]

3.q: וְ⁠נִגְרְעָ֤ה נַחֲלָתָ⁠ן֙ מִ⁠נַּחֲלַ֣ת אֲבֹתֵ֔י⁠נוּ וְ⁠נוֹסַ֕ף עַ֚ל נַחֲלַ֣ת הַ⁠מַּטֶּ֔ה
3.note: The expressions **will be taken away** and **will be added** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and their husbands will take their inheritance away from the inheritance of our fathers, and they will add it to the inheritance of the tribe]

The leaders are using the term **fathers** to mean “ancestors.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. This also occurs in verse 8. Alternate translation: [from the inheritance of our ancestors]

The leaders are using **that they will be for them** as a common expression of the culture to mean “into which they will marry.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. This also occurs in verse 4. Alternate translation: [the tribe into which they will marry]

Here, **lot** represents “the portion of land that was assigned by lot.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And from the portion of land that was assigned to us by lot as our inheritance]

4.q: וְ⁠אִם יִהְיֶ֣ה הַ⁠יֹּבֵל֮ לִ⁠בְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וְ⁠נֽוֹסְפָה֙ נַחֲלָתָ֔⁠ן עַ֚ל נַחֲלַ֣ת הַ⁠מַּטֶּ֔ה
4.note: The leaders are speaking as if this were a hypothetical possibility, but they mean that it is actually true. The Jubilee would certainly come. If your language does not state something as a condition if it is certain or true, or if your readers might think that what the leaders are saying is uncertain, then you could translate this as a confident statement. Alternate translation: [And when the Jubilee comes for the sons of Israel, their inheritance will be added upon the inheritance of the tribe]

The **Jubilee** was a kind of special year that occurred every fiftieth year, when land that had been sold was returned to the family that originally owned it. If your readers would not be familiar with what the Jubilee was, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [the special fiftieth year for giving land back to its original owners]
See how you translated the similar expression in 26:55. This also occurs in verse 7. This also occurs in verses 6–8.

5.note: Here, **tribe** represents “the leaders of the tribe” who spoke to Moses. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [The leaders from the tribe of the sons of Joseph are speaking rightly]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:16.

6.note: This could mean: (1) that they can marry into any clan within the tribe of their father. Alternate translation: [only to any clan of the tribe of their father] (2) that they can marry only someone from the same clan as their father. Alternate translation: [only to the same tribe and clan as their father]

6.q: לֵ⁠אמֹ֔ר לַ⁠טּ֥וֹב בְּ⁠עֵינֵי⁠הֶ֖ם תִּהְיֶ֣ינָה לְ⁠נָשִׁ֑ים אַ֗ךְ לְ⁠מִשְׁפַּ֛חַת מַטֵּ֥ה אֲבִי⁠הֶ֖ם תִּהְיֶ֥ינָה לְ⁠נָשִֽׁים
6.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [that to the good in their eyes they will be for wives, only to the clan of the tribe of their father they will be for wives]

Moses is using **To the good in their eyes** as a common expression of the culture to mean “to whomever they think is best.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [To whomever they consider best]

7.q: וְ⁠לֹֽא תִסֹּ֤ב נַחֲלָה֙ לִ⁠בְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִ⁠מַּטֶּ֖ה אֶל מַטֶּ֑ה
7.note: Here Moses is speaking as if an inheritance were able to **go around** from one tribe to another. It means that land must not pass from the ownership of one tribe to another tribe. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And the ownership of an inheritance for the sons of Israel shall not pass from one tribe to another tribe]

Moses is not referring to a specific **man**. He means men in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [each person in the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers]

Here Moses is speaking as if each Israelite would **cling** to the inheritance of his ancestral tribe. It means that each Israelite would keep the land that belonged to his ancestral tribe. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [shall remain]

8.note: As in verse 6, his could mean: (1) that the woman can marry into any clan within the tribe of her father. Alternate translation: [from any clan of the tribe of her father] (2) that the woman can marry only someone from the same clan as her father. Alternate translation: [from the same tribe and clan as her father]

9.note: Moses is not referring to a specific **man**. He means each person among **the tribes of the sons of Israel**. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [each person]

11.note: Your language may have its own term or expression for this relationship. The phrase **the sons of their uncles** refers to the sons of their father’s brothers. Alternate translation: [to their cousins on their father’s side]

12.q: וַ⁠תְּהִי֙ נַחֲלָתָ֔⁠ן עַל מַטֵּ֖ה מִשְׁפַּ֥חַת אֲבִי⁠הֶֽן
12.note: The author is using **their inheritance was upon** as a common expression of the culture to mean “their inheritance remained with.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and their inheritance stayed with the tribe of the clan of their father]

13.q: אֵ֣לֶּה הַ⁠מִּצְוֺ֞ת וְ⁠הַ⁠מִּשְׁפָּטִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה
13.note: This verse is a comment that summarizes **the commandments and the ordinances** that Yahweh gave in the preceding chapters. This signals the end of the book of Numbers. Use the natural form in your language for expressing the conclusion of a story. Alternate translation: [In conclusion, these are the commandments and the ordinances that Yahweh commanded]

The terms **commandments** and **ordinances** mean similar things. Moses is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [all the commands]
